Luka Doncic's real estate

Luka Doncic's net worth has grown steadily since he turned pro as a teenager in Europe, and the numbers behind that rise tell their own story about how far his game has taken him. The Lakers guard signed a new contract extension in August 2025, the latest step in a financial climb that started long before he ever wore an NBA jersey.That jump followed a career path few players match. Doncic turned pro at 16 with Real Madrid, won EuroLeague MVP at 18, and became the youngest player in NBA history to post a 30-point triple-double as a teenager. Every stop added another layer to the fortune he has built since.According to Celebrity Net Worth, Doncic's fortune sits at $100 million as of 2026. Most of that total traces back to basketball paychecks, first from Real Madrid and now from NBA contracts that have made him one of the league's highest earners.Endorsements make up the rest. Nike signed him as a teenager in 2017, and Air Jordan built a signature shoe line around him two years later, the Jordan Luka 1. Air Jordan extended that deal for six more years in 2023, a sign of how much value the brand sees in his game beyond the box score.Doncic's income breaks down into two main streams:NBA salary. His rookie deal in Dallas gave way to a five-year, $207 million supermax extension in 2021, the largest guaranteed rookie extension in league history at the time.The February 2025 trade to the Lakers reset that number again, and his new deal now pays him $55 million a season.Brand deals. Nike and Air Jordan anchor his endorsement income, and a Doncic rookie card sold for $4.6 million in March 2021, the highest price ever paid for an NBA player card.Basketball still pays the bulk of the bills, but the card sale showed how much collectors value his early career on its own.The $207 million supermax extension Doncic signed with Dallas in August 2021 remains the largest deal of his career on paper, even after the Lakers trade. His new three-year, $165 million Lakers contract adds another major payday, with the $55 million annual salary marking a $15 million raise from what he made in Dallas.Between the Mavericks extension, the Lakers deal, and nearly a decade of European club pay before he ever set foot in the NBA, Doncic's on-court earnings alone account for the majority of his $100 million net worth.Doncic bought his first major property in 2020, a 5,225-square-foot home in Dallas for $2.7 million, built in 1984 and sitting on a .78-acre lot near Mavericks owner Mark Cuban. The house has four bedrooms, four and a half bathrooms, and a pool.After the trade to Los Angeles, Doncic paid $25 million in September 2025 for a Manhattan Beach mansion previously owned by tennis star Maria Sharapova, giving him a West Coast base to match his new team and a fresh chapter in a real estate portfolio that keeps growing alongside his game.

Most of that total traces back to basketball paychecks, first from real madrid and now from nba contracts. His income breaks down into two main streams: nba salary, endorsements, brand partnerships.

Article Title: 'I was India's 12th man for two years': Ajinkya Rahane reveals toughest phase of his career
Article Text:
Ajinkya Rahane

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former India batter Ajinkya Rahane has spoken about the difficult wait before making his Test debut, revealing that he spent two years travelling with the team as the 12th man. Rahane made his international debut in limited-overs cricket in 2011 but had to wait for 20 Test matches before finally getting his first chance in the longest format.Instead of feeling disappointed, he said he used the period to learn from his teammates and improve himself.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Rahane said: "The first two years, when I entered the team for the first time in 2011. I had to wait 20 games for my Test debut, and I was there as a 12th man for two years. That was a challenging phase, but I learnt a lot from it.""I had two choices: either to gain sympathy or try to improve myself. There is nothing bad about being a 12th man or serving water or helping your teammates. I took it positively.""I would look at everything, and because of that, I could play for a long time. Observing helped my attitude and mindset. It would be easy to gain sympathy, but I never expected that."Rahane also said patience was not something he had naturally when he started his career."It was there from before, but it also developed as I kept playing and gained experience.I will not say I had so much patience right from the start," Rahane said."When you travel in a local train in Mumbai, it is challenging. So somewhere, patience develops right from there. When I started domestic cricket and kept scoring consistently, you unknowingly think that your name should come for India. And even I thought the same," he said."But after talking to some senior players and over time, I realised it will happen when it has to happen. You do whatever is in your control. If you want to play for long, patience is important," he added.Rahane, who recently announced his retirement from all forms of cricket, scored 5,077 runs in 85 Tests at an average of 38.46, including 12 centuries and 26 half-centuries. He also played 90 ODIs, scoring 2962 runs at an average of 35.26, including 3 hundreds and 24 fifties. He also featured in 20 T20Is for India.
Article Summary: Ajinkya rahane reveals he spent two years travelling with the team as the 12th man. Rahane made his international debut in limited-overs cricket in 2011. He scored 5,077 runs in 85 tests at an average of 38.46, including 12 centuries.

Article Title: 'Jasprit Bumrah should take a break': Ex-India pacer urges selectors to consider Mohammed Shami and Bhuvneshwar Kumar
Article Text:
Jasprit Bumrah

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With Jasprit Bumrah ruled out of India's two-Test series against Sri Lanka, starting August 15, because of a knee injury, former India fast bowler Karsan Ghavri has called for the return of experienced pacers Mohammed Shami and Bhuvneshwar Kumar . Ghavri believes India should not depend only on Bumrah and should use senior bowlers to reduce the workload on the star fast bowler.Shami impressed for Bengal in the Ranji Trophy last season, taking 37 wickets, while Bhuvneshwar claimed 28 wickets during Royal Challengers Bengaluru's IPL 2026 title-winning campaign.Speaking to Mid-Day, Ghavri said both bowlers have shown they are fit and deserve another chance."Shami and Bhuvi have been playing consistently in the IPL without injuries and should return to the national set-up. Selectors should consider them," Ghavri said."All fast bowlers face niggles or injuries, but Bumrah has been on and off for the last two-three years. He has hardly played an entire series. That's not a good sign for him or for the country," he said.Ghavri also suggested that Bumrah should take a long break to fully recover instead of returning before he is completely fit."Bumrah should take a break for five to six months or even a year, and get back to 100 per cent fitness.The issue is that he goes into tournaments even if he's half-fit and then, due to workload management, halfway through, there's a breakdown. This is unnecessary. Only if he can manage his workload throughout a tournament should he be included in the team."Ghavri said India should focus on using Bumrah mainly in Test cricket while sharing the workload with Shami, Mohammed Siraj and Bhuvneshwar."I don't think Bumrah can sustain playing all formats. The team management must consider playing him only in Tests as that's a critical format," Ghavri said."Though he may want to play IPL, T20Is and ODIs too, it's not viable. For this reason, it will be great if Mohammed Siraj can get the support of senior pacers like Shami and Bhuvi," the former pacer said."Bhuvi should be used in T20Is because he's done brilliantly in the IPL. And you can rotate Shami and Siraj in Tests. This will reduce the pressure on Bumrah," he said.
Article Summary: Jasprit bumrah ruled out of india's two-test series against sri lanka. Former india fast bowler karsan ghavri has called for the return of experienced pacers mohammed shami and bhuvneshwar kumar. Shami impressed for bengal in the ranji trophy last season, taking 37 wickets.

What Detroit gets in return

Miami Heat's frontcourt build around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo has left little room to add complementary shooting, but a hypothetical deal with the Detroit Pistons could change that. The Heat are reportedly eyeing a swap that would send Nikola Jovic to Detroit in exchange for Duncan Robinson, the sharpshooter who spent his first seven NBA seasons in Miami before departing last summer.Robinson signed a three-year, $48 million deal with the Pistons via sign-and-trade last July, and his $15.99 million cap figure in 2026-27 lines up closely with Jovic's salary, making the framework realistic on paper. With Miami already having sacrificed backcourt depth to land Antetokounmpo, adding a proven floor-spacer like Robinson would address one of the roster's clearest gaps, and speculation around a reunion is starting to build.Robinson, 32, is coming off a career-best role with the Pistons, starting all 77 games he played and averaging 12.2 points on 45.6 percent shooting while knocking down 41.0 percent of his threes, numbers that helped power Detroit to a 60-win season. He's not a shot-creator or a high-usage scorer; his value is as an off-screen floor spacer who forces defenses to stay honest away from the ball.That profile is exactly what Miami is missing. The Heat gave up backcourt shooting in Tyler Herro and Norman Powell to build around Antetokounmpo, and while Tim Hardaway Jr.helps, a second reliable movement shooter like Robinson would let the Heat surround their new frontcourt pairing with more spacing on a night-to-night basis.The proposed framework, according to Heavy.com, is a straight swap: Robinson heads back to Miami, and Detroit takes on Nikola Jovic plus two future second-round picks. It keeps the deal to two teams and avoids the logistical headaches of a larger, multi-team structure.Miami's need is straightforward. The roster already lost shooting depth in the moves that brought in Antetokounmpo, and the front office has been looking to balance the frontcourt-heavy core with more perimeter spacing ever since.Detroit's side makes sense too. The Pistons have shown through their offseason moves that they're prioritizing flexibility, and taking on a younger piece in Jovic while adding draft capital fits that direction, even as they'd be moving on from a starter who helped them to 60 wins.Miami Heat receive: Duncan RobinsonDetroit Pistons receive: Nikola Jovic, 2027 second-round pick, 2031 second-round pickRobinson gives the Heat a second high-volume, high-percentage shooter alongside Tim Hardaway Jr., which fills the biggest hole left after trading away backcourt shooting to acquire Antetokounmpo. Slotted next to Antetokounmpo, Adebayo, Andrew Wiggins and Hardaway Jr., Robinson rounds out a lineup with frontcourt size, wing defense and reliable outside shooting in one group.Financially, the framework is clean. Robinson's $15.99 million cap hit for 2026-27 is close enough to Jovic's that the trade works as a near-even salary swap, without Miami needing to attach further money to balance the books.Detroit adds Jovic, a young piece the Heat had hoped to develop long-term, giving the Pistons a lower-cost option on their books going forward. Paired with the two second-round picks (2027 and 2031), the return leans toward future assets and flexibility, in line with how Detroit has approached its offseason.Losing Robinson's shooting off a 60-win roster is a real cost, but taking back a younger, cheaper player plus draft capital keeps the Pistons' books lighter beyond this season.Robinson slots in as an immediate shooting fix around a star-heavy core at a manageable cap number, while Detroit's return leans more on long-term flexibility than immediate production.

Article Title: “Not everyone gets those same opportunities”: How Patrick Mahomes turned a young fan’s dream into an unforgettable Super Bowl moment in Las Vegas
Article Text:

Patrick Mahomes turned a simple interview into a once-in-a-lifetime Super Bowl surprise

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick Mahomes has built his reputation on dramatic comebacks and championship performances, but one of his most meaningful moments came away from the football field. In early 2024, the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback surprised young fan Isaac Murdock with tickets to Super Bowl LVIII in Las Vegas through his 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, creating a memory that reached far beyond sports.What made the surprise even more special was that Isaac never saw it coming. Born with a rare spinal defect that resulted in paraplegia, he had arrived at the Chiefs’ practice facility believing he was there for an interview connected to Mahomes’ foundation. Instead, the visit became a life-changing experience that showed why the Chiefs star often speaks about using his platform to create opportunities for children.Before the surprise was revealed, Isaac was asked what he admired most about Patrick Mahomes. His answer captured the reason so many young fans look up to the quarterback. “Mainly just his attitude and how he approaches the game. He’s humble,” Isaac said.Moments later, Mahomes walked into the room and greeted him with a smile. On behalf of the Kansas City Chiefs and the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, he revealed that Isaac and his family would be attending Super Bowl LVIII in Las Vegas.The young fan could hardly believe what he had just heard. “This is crazy,” Isaac The emotional moment was filmed and later featured in an NFL Network segment connected to Mahomes’ Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year nomination. Yet the interaction quickly became about much more than football tickets.Isaac continues to play basketball and dreams of working in sports broadcasting one day. Mahomes said that determination stood out to him throughout their conversation.“Isaac’s not going to let that hurt him. Whatever his dream is, he’s going to go out there and maximize it and there’s going to be a smile on his face the entire time,” Mahomes said.The quarterback also spoke about Isaac’s interest in broadcast school and how important it was for him to encourage those ambitions.“We were talking about he wants to go to broadcast school and he wants to be a part of sports in some way,” Mahomes said. “I’m glad that I’m able to help give him an opportunity to go to the Super Bowl and enjoy that and see it.”The surprise reflected the larger mission of the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, which focuses on improving children’s lives through health, wellness and support for communities in need.Patrick Mahomes explained why those efforts matter deeply to him. “I realize how blessed I am to be able to go out and play football and follow my dreams. Not everyone gets those same opportunities,” he said. He followed that with a message that captured the heart of the entire moment.“You don’t know which kid’s going to impact the world positively, and you want to make sure every kid has those opportunities.”For NFL fans, Patrick Mahomes is often defined by Super Bowl victories and spectacular throws. For Isaac Murdock, he became the person who turned admiration into encouragement and transformed an ordinary visit into an unforgettable Super Bowl memory in Las Vegas.
Article Summary: Patrick mahomes surprised young fan isaac murdock with tickets to super bowl lviii in las vegas. Isaac was born with a rare spinal defect that resulted in paraplegia. The chiefs quarterback often speaks about using his platform to create opportunities for children.

Article Title: BCCI to standardise Bronco, 2K base fitness test parameters after England tour debacle
Article Text:
Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana

BCCI pulls up lacklustre fitness tests

Communication breakdown

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Injury prevention lost priority

NEW DELHI: Flustered by the frequent injury breakdowns of players in the Indian team, the medical team at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru is looking to resurrect its fitness programme. TOI understands that the CoE is finally working on standardising base fitness parameters after it emerged that the non-definitive customised fitness tests for players were identified as a core reason for the drop in the overall fitness standards.The Indian team went through a change in fitness testing drills after Adrian Leroux replaced Soham Desai as the strength and conditioning coach last year. It is learnt that the BCCI medical team, which includes the CoE and the Indian team, has struggled to work in sync to assess the fitness of players. Since Leroux took over, it was decided that the Bronco test would be the primary test to judge fitness instead of the Yo-Yo test.The Bronco test, which is a more agility driven test, didn’t have a base parameter till now. TOI has learnt that the BCCI medical team has rolled out a figure of 5.15-5.20 minutes as a base figure to complete the assorted drills to be declared fit enough to be selected after the debacle in white-ball tour of Ireland and England.Earlier, the BCCI had set 16.5 as a marker to clear the basic Yo-Yo test. The CoE has also set 9-10 minute mark to complete the 2 km running test which is known as the 2K test.“The Indian players are not used to the Bronco test. Over the last year, the CoE had set different base parameters for players. It has now emerged that certain senior players were given much comfortable targets to meet to clear fitness tests. The CoE staff had also cleared players like Harshit Rana and Nitish Kumar Reddy to make sure it was delivering players according to team management’s needs,” a BCCI source told TOI.TOI has learnt that the team management and BCCI, led by secretary Devajit Saikia, has questioned Team India physio Kamlesh Jain for the repeated breakdowns and overall dip in the fitness standards. The team management is also not happy with players cramping so frequently even in the favourable English weather.“Kamlesh has been told that he shouldn’t worry about any player’s stature and flag anything that he doesn’t find satisfactory. It has been seen that the mobility of some of the players in the field has been questionable. Senior batters are struggling to push their running between the wickets as they bat longer. The number of slow fielders has increased,” the source said.It has been observed that regular India players have not been prepared for the new fitness drills. For instance, someone like Mohammed Siraj was recently caught off guard by the sudden fitness tests at CoE before leaving for Sri Lanka.“It is only now that contracted players have been handed the base parameters of the new tests. The Test regulars were caught off guard by the programme given to them at CoE. The players who are not part of the Test team are now starting to work according to the base parameter,” the source said. The CoE failed to get Jasprit Bumrah ready despite the selectors and the team management were assured that he would be fit for the first Test in Sri Lanka on Aug 15.In the case of Harshit Rana, which has been an embarrassment for the CoE since he had just recovered from a knee injury, there was no clear messaging about the desired fitness levels. TOI understands that Rana had suffered severe cramps and not any injury when he was sent back to the CoE from England after the third T20I. It was cited that he was overweight.“The Indian team management flagged that he was overweight by four kgs. The CoE should have been much more vigilant. He has been now told by CoE staff that his weight can’t exceed 96 kgs. He is now 94 kgs and is expected to be cleared next week. But he was 97 kgs when he was cleared to be picked for the Indian team for the UK tour,” the source said.The Indian team management had finally got it right when it managed to play three consecutive ICC events — the 2023 ODI World Cup, 2024 T20 World Cup and 2025 Champions Trophy — with all resources available. Only Hardik Pandya suffered an injury after twisting his ankle in the 2023 World Cup. BCCI had devised an impeccable injury management programme and customised for each player.TOI understands that the fitness programmes have drifted away from prevention to a more rigorous approach. “Now, a player at CoE is made to take a 2K test and Bronco test more frequently besides the Yo-Yo test which burns out players. Earlier, it was about maintaining certain fitness marks for players without burning them out with fitness regimes. Yo-Yo tests were designed to be taken in six months or if a player is coming back from injury. The other management had made notes of pressure points for each player and accordingly regulated the workload. Now, the players are just pushed to do extreme fitness programmes,” the source claimed.
Article Summary: The indian team went through a change in fitness testing drills after adrian leroux replaced soham desai as the strength and conditioning coach last year. Since leroux took over, it was decided that the bronco test would be the primary test to judge fitness instead of the yo-yo test.

Article Title: 'I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan': Arshad Nadeem blames Glasgow cold for CWG poor show
Article Text:
Arshad Nadeem (AFP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lausanne Diamond League next

Pakistan’s Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem has blamed the cold Glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the Commonwealth Games. The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds, saying the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.Nadeem managed 77.41 metres with his second throw after opening with a foul. His third attempt was 75.39m, leaving him outside the top eight.“The weather was extremely cold and I personally felt that it affected my body. As you have seen in many of my previous competitions, my run-up is usually very smooth, but this time it wasn’t… because my body had become stiff due to the cold conditions. My fitness was good and my health was fine, but ultimately whatever Allah wills is what happens,” he told reporters on Wednesday.Despite the result, Nadeem said he remains determined to make a strong comeback and urged fans to continue supporting him.“Please don’t lose heart and don’t stop supporting me either. Whatever I have achieved has only been possible because Allah blessed me with the opportunity to do it. The respect and recognition Pakistan has received around the world have come through years of hard work. I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan,” he added.“God willing, I will prepare with full dedication for the upcoming competitions and once again raise Pakistan’s flag on the international stage.”Nadeem also responded to criticism on social media, saying he understood the disappointment among Pakistani fans.“I have heard many things on social media, but I want everyone to remember that I am Pakistan’s son, and I always will be,” he maintained.Nadeem’s next challenge will be the Lausanne Diamond League in Switzerland on August 21. He will face a strong field that includes India’s Neeraj Chopra , Commonwealth champion Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, Keshorn Walcott, Anderson Peters and Thomas Rohler.Nadeem will hope to regain his form before the Asian Games later this year.
Article Summary: Olympic javelin champion arshad nadeem has blamed the cold glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the commonwealth games. The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds. He said the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.

Article Title: 'Neeche baith ke rah': Yashasvi Jaiswal recalls Rohit Sharma's stump-mic scolding in Instagram post
Article Text:
Photo/screengrab

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India opener Yashasvi Jaiswal looked back at a memorable moment involving former captain Rohit Sharma as the team prepared for the upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka.Jaiswal shared a set of pictures from India's training session as preparations began for the two-Test series. However, it was his caption that caught the attention of fans.The left-handed batter referred to one of Rohit's well-known on-field instructions from India's tour of Australia."Because once a legend said 'jab tak khelega nahi, tab tak uthneka nahi'," Jaiswal wrote on Instagram.The caption was a reference to an incident during the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy. Jaiswal was fielding at forward silly point when he briefly stood up before Steve Smith had completed his shot.Rohit, who was captaining India at the time, noticed it immediately and reminded Jaiswal to stay low until the ball had been played.“Ae Jaisu, gully cricket khel raha hai kya? Neeche baith ke rah (“Are you playing gully cricket? Stay down. Don’t get up until the ball has been played!)” Rohit was heard saying on the stump microphone.The exchange quickly went viral and became one of the lighter moments of India's tour of Australia.Jaiswal's Instagram post brought back memories of that moment as India prepare for the Sri Lanka series.The Shubman Gill-led team has started training in Colombo ahead of the two-match Test series. Jaiswal is expected to open the batting with KL Rahul when India face Sri Lanka in the first Test at the Galle International Stadium on August 15.
Article Summary: Yashasvi jaiswal posted a picture of india's training session on instagram. The left-handed batsman referred to an on-field incident involving rohit sharma. The former captain reminded him to stay low during a match in australia. India face sri lanka in a two-test series starting on august 15.

Article Title: Why Ireland must now play qualifiers for the 2027 ODI World Cup
Article Text:
Ireland cricket team (Pic credit: Cricket Ireland)

Why Ireland missed direct qualification

How Ireland can still reach the 2027 World Cup

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ireland's hopes of securing direct qualification for the 2027 ICC Men's ODI World Cup were washed away on Wednesday after persistent rain forced the opening ODI against Afghanistan in Bready to be abandoned without a ball being bowled.The washout officially ended Ireland's already slim mathematical chance of climbing into the automatic qualification spots in the ICC ODI rankings before the September 30, 2026 cut-off date, meaning they must now take the longer route to the World Cup through the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier.Currently ranked 12th in the ODI rankings, Ireland needed an extraordinary sequence of results to qualify directly. They had to complete a 5-0 clean sweep over Afghanistan while also hoping West Indies lost both of their remaining ODIs against India. With the first match abandoned, that possibility disappeared.The 2027 ODI World Cup, to be jointly hosted by South Africa and Zimbabwe, will feature 12 teams.Hosts South Africa and Zimbabwe qualify automatically, while the remaining direct qualification spots are decided through the ICC ODI rankings at the September 30 cut-off.Ireland's ranking left them outside the automatic qualification places, and only a dramatic rise through a series whitewash over Afghanistan, coupled with favourable results elsewhere, could have changed their fate.The abandoned match in Bready ensured that Ireland could no longer gain enough ranking points to overtake Afghanistan, West Indies and Zimbabwe before the deadline.Despite missing direct qualification, Ireland remain firmly in contention for the tournament through the qualification pathway.They will compete in the 10-team ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier, where the stakes are high. The tournament winner will earn a direct place in the 12-team World Cup.Teams finishing second, third and fourth will advance to the World Cup Super Series, where they will battle for the final available spot in the main tournament.The Qualifier will feature the two lowest-ranked Full Member nations in the ODI rankings — excluding hosts South Africa and Zimbabwe — along with the top four teams from the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2 and four teams emerging from the World Cup Qualifier Playoff.The Playoff itself will include the bottom four sides from League 2 and four teams from the ICC Challenge League. The top four teams from that competition will progress to the Qualifier.The Challenge League consists of 12 teams split into two groups of six, with each group playing three round-robin tournaments during the qualification cycle. The top two teams from each group will advance to the Playoff.Ireland will be determined to avoid a repeat of the heartbreak they suffered ahead of the 2023 ODI World Cup, when they were eliminated in the Super Six stage of the Qualifier and failed to book a place at the tournament in India. With direct qualification now out of reach, their road to the 2027 World Cup will once again depend on navigating the demanding qualifying route.
Article Summary: Ireland's hopes of direct qualification for the 2027 icc men's odi world cup were washed away on wednesday. The opening odi against afghanistan in bready was abandoned without a ball being bowled. The washout officially ended ireland's already slim mathematical chance of climbing into the automatic qualification spots in the icc odi rankings before the september 30, 2026 cut-off date.

Argentina's Football Association (AFA) has unanimously approved July 15 as "National Football Teams Day" to mark the national team's comeback win over England in the 2026 FIFA World Cup semifinal.Argentina came from 1-0 down in the closing stages of the match to beat England 2-1 and qualify for their second straight World Cup final. The NFL confirmed the six-game suspension, but neither the league nor the Saints has explained what led to it.No verified report has identified a specific violation.So, if you are asking why Brock Rechsteiner is suspended for six games, the honest answer is straightforward: the NFL has announced the suspension, but it has not publicly disclosed the reason.The current situation creates another challenge for New Orleans. Article Title: NFL Hall of Fame 2026: Which five legends earned football’s highest honor in this year’s iconic class?
Article Text:
2026 nfl hall of fame class (NFL)

Who made the NFL Hall of Fame class of 2026?

Drew Brees

Roger Craig

Larry Fitzgerald

Luke Kuechly

Adam Vinatieri

The Pro Football Hall of Fame will add five more all-time greats to football's most exclusive club this weekend in Canton, Ohio. The celebration begins with the annual Hall of Fame Game featuring the Arizona Cardinals and Carolina Panthers, two franchises represented in this year's class. But the spotlight belongs to the players whose careers changed the game in different ways. Quarterback Drew Brees, running back Roger Craig, wide receiver Larry Fitzgerald, linebacker Luke Kuechly and kicker Adam Vinatieri will now take their place among the sport's greatest names after building legacies defined by consistency, impact and unforgettable moments.This year's Hall of Fame class features one quarterback, one running back, one wide receiver, one linebacker and one kicker, reflecting excellence across every phase of the game.Drew Brees' Hall of Fame journey is as much about resilience as it is about numbers.After beginning his career with the San Diego Chargers, Brees faced uncertainty following a devastating shoulder injury that included a torn labrum and partial rotator cuff tear. The Chargers moved forward with Philip Rivers, leaving Brees searching for another opportunity.That decision reshaped NFL history.Joining forces with Sean Payton in New Orleans, Brees transformed the Saints into one of the league's most productive offenses.He led the NFL in passing yards seven times and became the first quarterback to throw for at least 5,000 yards in four different seasons.His defining moment came in Super Bowl XLIV, where he guided New Orleans to its first championship and earned Super Bowl MVP honors. By the time he retired, Brees had accumulated 80,358 passing yards and 571 touchdown passes, both ranking second only to Tom Brady.Roger Craig's selection ends one of the longest waits among modern NFL stars.A cornerstone of San Francisco's dynasty during the 1980s, Craig brought versatility that was years ahead of its time. He helped the 49ers capture three Super Bowl titles while delivering seven straight seasons with at least 1,000 scrimmage yards.His 1985 season remains historic. Craig became the first running back in NFL history to record both 1,000 rushing yards and 1,000 receiving yards in the same year, setting a standard later generations of dual-threat backs would follow.Few receivers matched Larry Fitzgerald's consistency over nearly two decades.The former third overall pick spent all 17 seasons with the Arizona Cardinals and became the face of the franchise. He crossed the 1,000-yard mark six times during his first eight seasons and remained remarkably durable throughout his career.Fitzgerald finished with 17,492 receiving yards, second only to Jerry Rice, while his 121 touchdown receptions rank sixth in league history. He also helped Arizona reach Super Bowl XLIII, further strengthening a career that rarely lacked elite production.Luke Kuechly played only eight seasons, but few defenders dominated the position as completely.He won Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2012, Defensive Player of the Year the following season and collected five First-Team All-Pro selections. Kuechly never recorded fewer than 102 tackles in a season and added 18 interceptions through exceptional football intelligence and anticipation.Although a Super Bowl title escaped him, he was the heartbeat of Carolina's defense during its run to Super Bowl 50 and remains one of the smartest linebackers of his generation.Adam Vinatieri's place in Canton reflects more than longevity.The former Patriots and Colts kicker becomes only the third pure kicker inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Across 24 seasons, he converted an NFL-record 599 field goals while delivering some of the biggest kicks the league has ever witnessed.His last-second game-winning field goals in Super Bowls XXXVI and XXXVIII helped launch New England's championship era. Combined with four Super Bowl rings and nearly a quarter-century of consistency, Vinatieri built a résumé that many consider unmatched for a kicker.
Article Summary: This year's hall of fame class features one quarterback, one running back, one wide receiver, one linebacker and one kicker. Quarterback drew brees, running back roger craig, wide receiver larry fitzgerald, linebacker luke kuechly and kicker adam vinatieri will now take their place in canton.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “My dad told me I could do it when I was eight years old.” - How Coco Gauff turned family sacrifice and belief into Grand Slam glory
Article Text:

How did Coco Gauff’s parents help build her tennis dream?

How did Coco Gauff handle fame after her Wimbledon breakthrough?

Why was Coco Gauff’s 2023 US Open victory so emotional?

Why does Coco Gauff’s story inspire people beyond tennis?

When people talk about Coco Gauff today, they see a Grand Slam champion, an Olympic flag bearer for Team USA, and one of the biggest stars in tennis. But long before the trophies and worldwide fame, there was a little girl with a dream and two parents who believed in it without hesitation. Corey and Candi Gauff changed their own lives so their daughter could chase tennis full-time, even when there were no guarantees. Years later, that faith helped Coco reach the top of the sport, making her story about much more than winning titles.Coco Gauff’s journey began in Delray Beach, Florida, where she grew up in a family that loved sports. Her father, Corey Gauff, played college basketball, while her mother, Candi Gauff, competed in track and field before becoming a teacher.As Coco’s talent became impossible to ignore, her parents made a life-changing decision. Corey left his healthcare job so he could coach his daughter full-time. At the same time, Candi stepped away from teaching to homeschool Coco and manage her education around training and tournaments.It was a huge gamble. The family had to live on one income while spending time and money traveling across the United States for junior events.Even during difficult moments, her parents never stopped believing she could achieve something special.Looking back on those early years, Coco has often said their confidence gave her the courage to keep going.“My dad told me I could do it when I was eight years old. Obviously, you’re never 100% sure, but my parents believed in me from the start. That belief meant everything when I was growing up.”For Coco, those words became a foundation she carried with her as the competition became tougher and the expectations grew bigger.Everything changed in 2019 when a 15-year-old Coco arrived at Wimbledon.After earning a wild card into qualifying, she won her way into the main draw before facing five-time Wimbledon champion Venus Williams in the first round. Beating one of her childhood heroes instantly made her one of the biggest stories in world tennis.The sudden attention also brought enormous pressure. Every tournament came with questions about whether she could become the next great American champion.During that period, her family made sure tennis never became the only thing that defined her. Her mother regularly reminded her to separate the player from the person.Speaking about those conversations, Coco said:“My mom always tells me to just be Coco. She reminds me that tennis is just a game, and it doesn’t define who I am as a person. Having that perspective from my family keeps me sane.”That advice helped her stay grounded through both victories and disappointing defeats. Instead of trying to live up to outside expectations, she focused on improving one match at a time while keeping her family close.The family’s years of sacrifice came together in September 2023 at the US Open.Playing in front of a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd, 19-year-old Coco fought back after losing the opening set to defeat Aryna Sabalenka and win her first Grand Slam singles title.The final point brought an emotional celebration. Coco dropped to the court before running into the stands to hug her parents, who were both in tears after watching the dream they had shared for years become reality.During the trophy ceremony, she made sure the spotlight also belonged to the people who had stood beside her from the beginning.“Thank you to my parents. Today was the first time I ever saw my dad cry. He doesn’t want me to tell you that, but he did! He supported me from day one. My mom, she’s been my rock through everything. I’m just so grateful for them.”She also had a message for the critics who doubted whether she would reach the top of the game.“To those who thought they were putting water on my fire, you were really adding gas to it. Now I’m burning so bright.”Those words reflected years of hard work, setbacks and determination that led to one unforgettable night in New York.Coco Gauff’s success is often measured through her titles, rankings and achievements. Yet many people connect with her story because of what happened away from the tennis court.Her parents gave up stable careers so she could chase a dream. They supported her during uncertain years, protected her from outside pressure and reminded her that her value would never depend on winning matches.Coco has never forgotten those sacrifices. Whether speaking after major victories or reflecting on her childhood, she continues to credit her family for helping shape both the athlete and the person she has become.Her journey also shows that belief at home can change a young person’s future. Talent opened the first door, but the trust, patience and commitment shown by her family helped her keep moving forward when the road became difficult.Today, as one of the leading faces of women’s tennis, Coco continues to inspire young athletes who dream of following a similar path. Her story is proof that behind many great champions is a family willing to make difficult choices, stand by them through every challenge and keep believing long before the rest of the world does.
Article Summary: Coco gauff won her first grand slam singles title at the 2023 us open. She beat five-time wimbledon champion venus williams in the first round. The 19-year-old is now an olympic flag bearer for team usa. Her parents changed their lives so she could chase her tennis dream. Coco gauff's parents gave up stable careers so she could chase a dream.

Article Title: French trans basketball star Julie Tétart hopes to join WNBA following Sophie Cunningham’s controversial statement
Article Text:
Julie Tétart. Image via: Getty Images

Julie Tétart is eyeing a move to the WNBA

Julie Tétart dominated France's Ligue Féminine 2

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Julie Tétart's WNBA hopes gain spotlight amid Sophie Cunningham's comments

Julie Tétart, the French transgender basketball player who led her league in scoring and rebounding this past season, says she would accept a WNBA contract if one came her way. The comment surfaced as the league continues wrestling with a separate controversy involving Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, whose remarks opposing transgender participation in women's sports sparked protests, a suspension, and White House attention over the past several weeks.Tétart, who plays center for Monaco Basket Association in France's Ligue Féminine 2, told reporters she wasn't holding her breath but wouldn't turn down the opportunity either.Tétart's numbers from the 2025-26 LF2 season made the question worth asking. She averaged roughly 21 points and 20 rebounds per game, leading the league in both categories while playing at 6-foot-3. Despite that production, she was passed over for MVP, though she still collected Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, and Domestic Player of the Year honors.Asked directly whether she'd consider trying out for a WNBA roster, Tétart didn't dismiss it. "I won't say no," she said. She followed that by noting the realistic obstacles facing a 34-year-old crossing over from a second-tier European league, pointing out that plenty of players in the WNBA are simply better equipped for that level. “But you have to be realistic: I'm old, and there are far better players than me!" Tétart told OutKick.Her dominance wasn't limited to a strong statistical average. During one March game, Tétart posted 21 points and 30 rebounds, setting a new league rebounding record and breaking her own previous mark. Such production is part of why French trans advocacy groups pushed back hard when she was left off the league's MVP ballot, a decision that also excluded fellow trans player Aurore Pautou despite her own strong season.Tétart addressed the possibility of a WNBA future carefully, calling it a longtime aspiration shared by any young female basketball player, but adding that circumstances outside the sport make it unlikely. She pointed to broader political conditions in the United States, without going into detail, as the sticking point rather than anything about the league itself.The timing put Tétart's comments squarely inside an ongoing WNBA debate. Cunningham, a seventh-year guard for the Fever, drew national attention after telling ESPN she supports keeping transgender athletes out of girls' and women's sports, framing her stance as protective rather than hostile. She stood by the comments the next day, telling reporters, "I said what I said. I think it's kind of common sense."Not everyone in the league agreed. Fever head coach Stephanie White pushed back on framing exclusion as any kind of solution, saying, "I don't ever believe that exclusion is an answer," while acknowledging she didn't consider herself well-versed in the underlying science. Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve went further, later telling reporters, "I come from a space of inclusion," and wearing a shirt reading "Trans Kids Belong" during a game against Indiana.Whether Tétart ever gets an actual roster offer remains an open question. For now, her answer stands on record, and the league's ongoing debate over transgender inclusion shows no sign of settling before training camps open.
Article Summary: Julie tétart led france's ligue féminine 2 in scoring and rebounding this season. The 34-year-old center says she would accept a wnba contract if one came her way. Her comments come amid the wnba's ongoing debate over transgender inclusion.
